title: S2 workspace identity and ledger behavioral oracle

scope.phase: S2 identity, repository fence, and durable ledger foundations
permittedBehavior: Pure domain validation for typed identifiers, root aliases, and relative paths
Engine contracts for repository identity and exclusive fencing
Adapter identity resolution and authoritative ledger binding
Forward-only transactional schema migration and additive ledger persistence
excludedBehavior: Changing the default worktree root or selecting a root without explicit configuration
Deleting, relocating, or rewriting existing runs, events, attempts, evidence, or Git state
Guessing ownership for legacy paths or automatically binding legacy records to a repository
Activating runtime producers, cleanup, restart, recovery, retention, or destructive lifecycle behavior

preconditions: A valid v4 database contains multiple run rows, events, attempts, evidence payloads, feedback, and quota state.
Legacy worktree paths cannot be authoritatively associated with a repository identity.
cases.action: Open the database using the S2 adapter and migrate to v5.
expected: Migration commits schema version 5 and only adds the lifecycle schema required by S2.
Every preexisting row and payload in runs, events, attempts, evidence, routing_feedback, and quota_state is preserved byte-for-byte where stored as text and value-for-value otherwise.
Legacy ownership/path rows remain explicitly unbound or unresolved; no repository identity, root alias, or owner is inferred from path strings, basenames, branch names, or configuration.
Existing run roots and worktree paths are not rewritten or relocated.
noSideEffects: No deletes, updates, or replacements of existing history rows.
No filesystem or Git mutations outside the database migration.
failureInvariants: Any unpreservable legacy value aborts migration without partial v5 state.

preconditions: Separate fixture databases represent each supported legacy schema version 1, 2, and 3.
The implementation declares an explicit compatibility path and preservation mapping for each version it supports.
cases.action: Open each fixture and request migration to v5.
expected: Each version with a declared migration path follows that exact path transactionally and preserves all data represented by that source schema.
Any version without a declared and implemented compatibility path is rejected before writes; it is never promoted by changing only a version number.
The result for versions 1, 2, and 3 is individually observable and deterministic.
noSideEffects: Unsupported-version refusal leaves schema, rows, and database identity unchanged.
failureInvariants: No implicit compatibility assumption or destructive downgrade/upgrade guessing.

preconditions: A database has a schema version greater than 5 and contains sentinel schema objects and rows.
Capture a logical snapshot of schema objects, metadata, all table rows, and relevant database identity before opening.
cases.action: Attempt to open the database with the S2 adapter.
expected: The adapter refuses the database as newer/incompatible before applying migration DDL.
noSideEffects: The captured logical schema and data snapshot is unchanged.
No WAL/journal-mode transition, schema write, version update, or replacement database is created as a side effect of the refusal.
failureInvariants: A refusal after any persistent schema/data mutation fails this oracle.

preconditions: A valid v4 fixture has sentinel rows in every existing table and a captured logical snapshot.
A deterministic fault injection point can fail after at least one v5 DDL statement and before migration commit.
cases.action: Run migration with the injected failure.
expected: Migration reports failure and the database remains a valid v4 database.
noSideEffects: No v5 tables/indexes/constraints or schema-version change persist.
All preexisting rows and database identity match the pre-migration snapshot.
failureInvariants: No partial migration state is accepted or silently retried as success.

preconditions: A main checkout and at least one linked worktree resolve through the same Git common directory and underlying directory file identity.
Both use one stored repository UUID and one authoritative ledger binding.
cases.action: Resolve identity independently from the main checkout and linked worktree, then request writable ledger access from both.
expected: Both resolve to the same repository identity based on common-directory filesystem identity plus UUID.
Both attach to the same authoritative ledger and the repository-scoped fence.
Their distinct worktree locations remain locations under one repository; they do not become separate repositories.
noSideEffects: Resolution does not move worktrees or rewrite Git metadata.
failureInvariants: Path-string equality alone cannot establish identity or authority.

preconditions: Two repositories have the same final directory name and may have the same configured UUID, but their canonical common-directory filesystem identities differ.
Each repository has a separate legitimate ledger binding.
cases.action: Resolve both repositories and request writable access.
expected: The repositories remain distinct; equal basenames do not merge identity, history, or ledger authority.
noSideEffects: Neither repository's identity or history is overwritten by the other.
failureInvariants: Basename, branch prefix, or path suffix matching is never sufficient identity evidence.

preconditions: A repository directory is copied to a different filesystem identity while retaining the original UUID.
The original repository and ledger remain available.
cases.action: Resolve and request writable ownership for the copied repository, then verify the original repository remains accessible.
expected: The copied UUID plus mismatching filesystem identity is classified as a conflict/ambiguous copy and fails closed for writable ownership.
The original repository keeps its identity, ledger binding, and writable access.
noSideEffects: No UUID rotation, ledger fork, rebinding, or mutation of either repository is automatic.
failureInvariants: The conflict must not strand or silently transfer the original authority.

preconditions: A repository already has one authoritative ledger binding recorded in protected local operational state.
An alternate database path or a replacement database file is presented for the same repository identity.
cases.action: Request writable ownership using the alternate path and then using the replacement database.
expected: The alternate path attaches only when it is proven to be the same authoritative database; otherwise writable ownership/lineage is refused.
A replacement database with matching repository metadata but no authoritative binding is refused for independent writable history.
The established authority remains intact and usable.
noSideEffects: No parallel history is initialized and no binding is silently replaced.
failureInvariants: Database path equality or copied metadata alone is not proof of shared authority.

preconditions: Two independent processes target the same repository fence.
The test runs on a filesystem with supported exclusive-lock semantics; a separate fixture simulates or detects unsupported/unknown locking semantics.
cases.action: Have process A acquire the repository fence while process B attempts acquisition; repeat with an unsupported/unknown filesystem result.
expected: While A holds the fence, B cannot acquire writable ownership.
After A releases it, B may acquire it, subject to a fresh authority and liveness check.
Unknown or unsupported lock semantics fail closed for writable ownership; no lock-file-exists heuristic is treated as an exclusive lock.
noSideEffects: Lock contention does not create independent ledgers or alter repository identity.
failureInvariants: Concurrent processes must never both observe successful exclusive ownership.

preconditions: Two independent fixtures inject an unavailable or unsupported native file-ID observation: one for the canonical Git common directory, and one for the authoritative ledger file.
Capture current registry existence/bytes, ledger binding, and relevant logical database state before each attempt.
cases.action: Attempt repository identity resolution and writable ledger binding for each fixture.
expected: Unavailable native file identity for either the common directory or ledger refuses writable ownership before a repository binding is created or changed.
Neither path equality nor a stored UUID alone is accepted as an identity fallback.
The original repository and authoritative ledger remain usable when the observation is restored.
noSideEffects: The common-directory failure creates or modifies no registry/manifest and no ledger binding.
The ledger-file failure leaves the existing protected registry bytes/binding and database rows/identity unchanged.
No fallback identity or ownership is written to errors, logs, events, evidence, or exported/default JSON.
failureInvariants: Unknown native identity fails closed before writable binding or registry mutation; no path-only or UUID-only fallback is permitted.

preconditions: Fixtures include valid and invalid typed IDs, canonical root aliases, relative paths, traversal paths, absolute paths, separator variants, and ambiguous alias mappings.
cases.action: Validate each value and serialize accepted lifecycle records, events, evidence, and default JSON.
expected: Valid IDs, registered aliases, and contained relative paths round-trip without normalization changing identity unexpectedly.
Traversal, absolute path, malformed ID, unknown/ambiguous alias, and root escape inputs are rejected before persistence.
Events, evidence, and default JSON use root aliases and relative paths and contain no absolute external root.
Only the protected local operational root registry may retain the canonical external root needed for reconciliation.
noSideEffects: Rejected values do not create or update lifecycle rows or leak paths to logs/errors/exports.
failureInvariants: No absolute external path is emitted in default serialized records or telemetry.

preconditions: A ledger has an accepted plan content hash and existing immutable generation, event, attempt, evidence, artifact, and dependency rows.
A candidate generation record is prepared with the accepted plan hash, and a second candidate record is prepared with a changed hash without a newly accepted plan.
cases.action: Append/store the candidate generation record with the accepted plan hash, then separately attempt to append/store a generation record with the changed plan hash against the same accepted plan binding.
expected: The ledger accepts a new distinct immutable generation record pinned to the accepted plan hash.
The ledger rejects a generation record with a changed plan hash when no newly accepted plan authorizes that hash.
Earlier generation rows and their event, attempt, evidence, artifact, and dependency references remain available and unchanged after both operations.
noSideEffects: No run-loop, restart, or CLI action is invoked; a rejected changed-hash append changes no rows and no history is reset/deleted.
failureInvariants: Graph, generation, attempt, and artifact identities remain distinct and cannot be conflated.

preconditions: A ledger fixture has valid artifacts across at least two generations, explicit artifact identities, locations by alias/relative path, and dependency edges including shared references.
The schema declares foreign-key relationships required by the ledger and enables enforcement on each connection.
cases.action: Insert records transactionally, close and reopen the store, load them, and attempt dangling artifact and dependency references.
expected: Valid artifacts and dependency edges round-trip exactly, including identity, generation, state, and portable location fields.
Dangling graph/generation/artifact/dependency references are rejected by enforced constraints.
A failed insert transaction leaves no partially inserted artifact/dependency graph.
noSideEffects: Round-trip does not collapse shared dependencies or rewrite artifact identity.
failureInvariants: No orphan or cross-generation association is accepted silently.

requiredExecutedTestCount.criterion: At least one test implementing every oracle case must execute; record per-case counts and outcomes in evidence. This is a future implementation gate, not a current execution claim.

actualCargoCheck.reason: This artifact freezes expected behavior before implementation; it makes no validation claim.
